description: A programme of investigation just to the south of the Roman walled town identified a complex of masonry buildings, including a corridor villa, two aisled buildings, and an unusual winged building. The function of this latter building is unknown, and at least one interpretation put forward is that it was a temple, it is roughly dated to the 2nd - 3rd CE. It was later cut through by an aisled building.
bibliography: Bowden, W. “Architectural Innovation in the Land of the Iceni: A New Complex near Venta Icenorum (Norfolk).” Journal of Roman Archaeology 24 (2011): 382–88.
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Caistor St Edmund Villa (Norfolk).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
